# Historical Requirements Are Explicit

## Statement

Requirements for history — which data, which time dimensions (valid time, transaction time), which reconstruction questions and which retention — shall be stated explicitly at the information layer before a history mechanism is chosen.

## Rationale

History mechanisms are expensive to change after go-live. Choosing [[System-Versioned History Table|system versioning]] when the business needs valid-time corrections — or vice versa — is a common and costly mistake.

## Implications

- Information models annotate history requirements per entity/attribute.
- The mechanism is selected with [[Database History Pattern Decision Tree]].

## Consequences

- Positive: right-sized history, fewer rebuilds.
- Negative: requires business stakeholders to answer temporal questions they rarely consider.

## Applicability

Operational and analytical data subject to audit, correction or regulatory reconstruction.

## Exceptions

Data without any history requirement is explicitly marked as "current-state only".
